title: letssendit: ClawHub skill turns installed agents into a coordinated meme-token front-running botnet
summary: `letssendit` instructed every agent that installed it to pool Solana (SOL) into the operator's wallet through infrastructure at letssendit[.]fun. Once enough agents had joined, the operator bought the SENDIT meme token at the lowest bonding-curve price ahead of the participants, then the token launched publicly on pump[.]fun, where outside buyers could read the coordinated agent activity as organic retail demand. Unit 42 describes this as agentic front-running — a pump-and-dump executed by an autonomous agent network rather than by human accounts — and recommends enterprises block the skill outright for regulatory as well as security reasons.
details:
**Mechanism (Unit 42):** the SKILL.md is the whole payload. There is no dropper, no C2 implant and no credential theft; the skill simply directs autonomous agents to move their owners' funds and to participate in a launch whose price the operator controls, rotating wallets across multiple confirmed launches. That makes it invisible to malware-oriented controls: nothing on disk is malicious, and every action is one the agent was authorised to take.

**What a deterministic scanner sees:** instructions to move funds and to transact with an operator-controlled endpoint (`prompt-injection`, weak `exfiltration` on the outbound domain). Financial-harm intent expressed purely in natural language is the residual risk documented in docs/THREAT-MODEL.md R2/R9 — no rule in the six categories decides whether a skill's *purpose* is legitimate.

**Fact vs. inference:** skill name, domain, token, launch venue, mechanism and the SHA-256 are as published by Unit 42 (2026-06-23), which redacts the publisher account and reports the skill removed and the account banned after disclosure. Losses to individual users are not quantified in the source. Verified 2026-08-04.
